title: StarWM: Self-Supervised Trained Attention Routing for Robust World Models
claim: Separating where-to-attend from what-to-extract with gradient-isolated streams yields world models robust to multiple distractor types.
layout: 2 panels: left block-arrow diagram with three colored streams, right scatter plot
description: The left panel is a method diagram. An observation o_t goes through an encoder into a Feature box. From there the diagram splits into three colored routes. A blue Dynamics Stream runs through Predictive Feature to a Dynamics Model, which takes the action a_{t-1}. A red X-Attn module is labeled 'where to attend' and 'trained only by self-supervised signals'. A green Residual Stream runs through Non-Predictive Feature. The red and green routes merge in a Spatial Composition box, which feeds a decoder that produces the reconstruction ô_t ('what to extract'). Double-slash marks show stop-gradient barriers. Small image thumbnails with a green triangle illustrate the observation and the reconstruction. The right panel is a scatter plot of VH (sequential) IQM against VHR (random) IQM, with a diagonal line. StarWM and StarWM-R sit at the top right, and the baselines sit off to the sides or low down.
caption: STARWM disentangles where-to-attend (X-Attn) from what-to-extract (reconstruction ˆot). Left: Self-supervised objective signals train a cross-attention module to localize predictable, action-conditional content, while the content of the attended regions is shaped by a reconstruction objective through a dual-stream decoder. Stop-gradient barriers (//) keep the two objectives from interfering. For detailed architecture diagram see Appendix B.1. Right: Interquartile mean (IQM) aggregated across 6 DMC tasks under sequential (VH) and random (VHR) video distractors, normalized by DreamerV3 clean performance (recovery ratio). STARWM and its variant are the only methods robust to both distractor types.
abstract: A robust world model must strike the balance between faithfully capturing environmental dynamics and abstracting away from irrelevant content. While reconstruction-based world models ensure faithful supervision, they misallocate representational capacity by pixel area rather than dynamics relevance for visual tasks, which can cause task-irrelevant content to dominate the learned representation. Alternatively, reconstruction-free methods avoid this bias but risk discarding possibly relevant information. We propose StarWM, which uses a cross-attention module trained on self-supervised dynamics to decide where reconstruction applies. A dual-stream decoder then restricts reconstruction to the attended regions, with stop-gradient barriers preventing interference between the two objectives. These components allows reconstruction to supervise the visual content of attended regions without contaminating the latent with non-predictive information. On DeepMind Control with dynamic video backgrounds, default (reward-free) StarWM achieves the strongest performance under random-frame distractors and substantially outperforms reconstruction-based baselines under sequential video. In addition, its reward-augmented variant matches or exceeds reconstruction-free methods on sequential video, achieving the highest overall return across all distractor regimes. Mechanistic probing confirms \starwm{} preserves state attributes with near-perfect fidelity through long-horizon imagination while systematically discarding distractors. Code is available on GitHub.
